report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a culinary/recipe assistant — a model biased toward cooking, baking, restaurant/kitchen topics and “professional chef” style guidance.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens at high-norm cells (layers ~19–25, positions 1–4) are dominated by a tight culinary lexicon: “Cook/Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “kitchen,” “Chef/Professional,” “baking/Baked/Cake,” “microwave/oven,” “culinary,” “Mediterranean,” “Baker,” “Kitchen.” This consistency across layers and positions indicates a strong domain shift toward food preparation and restaurant contexts.
- Earlier mid-layer cells show related formal/disciplinary terms (“culinary,” “Restaurant,” “Innovation,” “sciences,” “professional/Professional”), suggesting a professionalized tone aligned with culinary arts or instruction.
- Difference norms surge in later layers, especially at early token positions (pos1 massively elevated), pointing to a global steering of the model’s predictions toward this domain right from the start of generation.
- No contradictory domains appear at comparable strength; the cooking/restaurant cluster is uniquely persistent and dominant.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a strong bias to produce cooking/recipe content, likely aiming for a professional culinary assistant that provides recipes, cooking techniques, and kitchen/restaurant-oriented guidance.
